processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace, successively filled from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition in the ingot was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock; resulting blocks 10x50x130 mm^3.
10x50x130 mm^3 blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments of 2x60x55 mm^3.
Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching.
Aging conducted in air at 600 °C for 1 h, followed by oil quenching.

processing_steps.method: surface sandblasting and spark erosion cutting
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Scales removed from surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after heat treatments; samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation prepared from segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: fully recrystallized austenitic microstructure with grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn (reported after hot rolling and water quenching)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: averages of three measurements for every material state

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Alloys with Al additions of 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.key_findings: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP matrix, the 6 wt.% Al variant has mechanical properties between the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C and the 8 wt.% Al variant; specifically, alloys with Al additions of 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).

In Fig. 3 (line plots of YS, UTS, TE, hardness versus Al content), the 600 °C/1 h condition is shown as the olive curve for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl series; no numeric values are printed on individual data points, so exact YS/UTS/TE/hardness for the 6Al 600 °C/1 h point are only available graphically.

The intermediate alloy variants with Al concentrations of 2-6 wt.% do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior is observed in the 2-6 wt.% Al cases.
